title: What color was it?
hook: A skeleton can leave some appearances unresolved.

knows: Illustrations can contain details absent from a fossil.
doesNotKnow: Separate an illustrated reconstruction from evidence of original coloration.

misconception: Every reconstruction color is directly recorded by the fossil.
objective: Separate an illustrated reconstruction from evidence of original coloration.

claims.text: A skeleton can leave some appearances unresolved. A dinosaur fossil preserves a skeleton but no identified pigment evidence. Can the skeleton alone establish its exact original color? The schematic skeleton does not include identified pigment evidence. Two different colors are shown as possibilities, not observations. Some fossils can preserve relevant pigment structures, but this example does not.

claims.text: The figure is a simplified, not-to-scale schematic of a stated example, not an image of an identified specimen.
Recall: A fossil has no identified pigment evidence. What should be said about the illustrated color? Without relevant evidence, the chosen color remains an illustrative possibility.
